memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Take one of the rams, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on its head. Slaughter it and take the blood and splash it against the sides of the altar. Cut the ram into pieces and wash the internal organs and the legs, putting them with the head and the other pieces. Then burn the entire ram on the altar. It is a burnt offering to the Lord, a pleasing aroma, a food offering presented to the Lord." - Exodus 29:15-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The first ram is a burnt offering, and the defining feature is in the word "entire." The whole animal goes up in smoke — nothing kept back, nothing reserved for the priests to eat, nothing retained. It was completely consumed and completely given.

God calls it "a pleasing aroma." There is something about total surrender that delights Him. Not because God enjoys destruction, but because wholehearted giving reflects the kind of love He desires. A partial offering says, "You may have this much." A whole burnt offering says, "You may have all of it."

Paul takes this exact image and applies it to us: offer your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God — this is your true and proper worship (Rom 12:1). The difference is that we are living sacrifices, which is harder in its own way, since a living sacrifice can always climb off the altar. Christ gave Himself completely for us as a fragrant offering (Eph 5:2). In grateful response, what is God asking you to stop holding back?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
What am I still holding back from God rather than offering entirely?
Does my life look like a partial offering or a whole one?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, Christ held nothing back from me. Show me what I am still reserving for myself, and give me the willingness to offer You all of it, not merely part. Amen.
